title.narrative: Världsbanken - Ethiopia Social Accountability Programme III 2019-2022
Worldbank - Ethiopia Social Accountability Programme III 2019-2022

description.narrative: Denna insats genomförs inom ramen för ett stort social service projekt som etiopiska regeringen och Världsbanken genomför. ESAP programmet bidrar till att främja dialog, deltagande och samarbete mellan de som ska erhålla service och de som levererar social service i syfte att göra öka kvalitet och kvantitet på servicen. Andra finansiärer till insatsen är USAID, Irish Aid, Austria Aid, EU and DfiD.
Support to improved service delivery at local level through strengthened dialogue and interaction between service providers and those receiving the services.

The expected result of the ESAP III is to 'Support strengthening the social accountability system and mechanisms for enhanced service delivery in Ethiopia' by - Expanding the uptake of social accountability tools including community empowerment and mobilization, community needs identification and prioritization processes, interface meetings and development of joint action plans. - Building capacity and systems strengthening to gradually institutionalize through sectors, CBOs, councils and other citizens' representative forums at federal, regional, woreda and community levels.

Ethiopian Social Accountability Program (ESAP) started by aiming implementation in 500 woredas of the country, however, due to shortfall in securing the necessary budget from DPs, the number of woredas reached so far is 416 woredas.
The citizen representation and the structure of the Woreda Social Accountability Committee (WSAC) is crucial to the well-functioning of the programme and its approach. Out of the 412 woredas, 410 have established WSACs.
ESAP3's shift of conducting social accountability at woreda level instead of the Kebele level has resulted in the increase of CBO members presence in the WSACs to ensure a sustainable committee that is dedicated to uplift the priorities of the community they serve.
Following this phase, ESAP will now be implemented by the Government of Ethiopia (GoE). GoE has received funding to institutionalize SA through the IDA20 funding, and has already started reforming the woreda staffing to include a SA focal person.
Based on the World Banks Implementation Completion and Results Report (ICR) for the Enhancing Shared Prosperity through Equitable Services (ESPES) program, the Ethiopia Social Accountability Program (ESAP) achieved several major results. Here are the key highlights:
•Coverage: ESAP expanded to 416 woredas, making it one of the largest social accountability programs in Africa. Out of these 416 woredas, the ESAP programme was implemented in 410 woredas in Ethiopia (99%), despite serious challenges in terms of security observed in the country. The remaining 1% were two woredas with serious security problems in Oromia and four contested woredas in Tigray region where the MA was not able to commence activities. Nearly 70% of target woredas have finished the entire SA cycle and others have progressed to latest steps, with 283 woredas reaching the JAP monitoring stage in 2023.
• Community Driven Accountability: Unlike topdown reforms, ESAP strengthens bottomup governance, empowering citizens to hold service providers accountable.
• Strong Role of Civil Society: Local CSOs play a key role in facilitating engagement, ensuring inclusivity, and bridging the gap between communities and government institutions. These CSOs were contracted with and supported by a Management Agency which played a key role in implementing ESAP, building methodologies, protocols and toolkits, while providing continuous technical support to the CSOs.
• Use of Social Accountability Tools: Methods like community scorecards and participatory budgeting provide structured ways for communities to voice concerns and propose solutions. 34% increase in community scorecard participation 13% increase in budget participation 18% more households in Joint Action Plans
• Focus on Marginalized Groups: ESAP ensures the participation of vulnerable groups, including women, persons with disabilities, and ethnic minorities. Special efforts were made to give these groups a stronger voice in decision making.
• Government Buy in and Institutionalization: The program is embedded within Ethiopias broader public sector reform efforts, enhancing its sustainability.
• Confidence in Local Councils: Over 66% of citizens expressed confidence in local councils ability to resolve community issues.
Overall, ESAP is reported to have contributed to improved service delivery, stronger citizen participation, building social cohesion, and promoting more responsive local governance, making it a model for social accountability initiatives in developing countries.
Challenges such as limited financial resources, weak technical capacity, and high staff turnover hindered effective implementation. Ethiopias decentralized governance model also created inconsistencies, as local governments lacked control over budgetary allocations from the central government.
The evaluation highlights that despite operational challenges, ESAP3 has laid a strong foundation for citizen driven governance reforms, demonstrating the potential of social accountability in enhancing public service deliver
